SUMMARY
( ) Draft ( X ) Final Environmental Statement Department of the Interior, Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife
1. Type of action: ( ) Administrative ( X ) Legislative
2. Brief description of action: To provide for the conservation, protection, and propagation of species and subspecies of fish and wildlife, domestic and foreign, that are threatened with extinction or likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction and gives the Secretary discretionary authority to regulate the taking of the latter group. The new program authorizes acquisition of land and water for endangered species without limitation as to cost; transfers from States to the Secretary authority to regulate the taking of all endangered species; prohibits U.S. subjects from taking endangered species on the high seas; increases penalties for civil violations from $5,000 to $10,000 and criminal violations from $10,000 to $20,000; provides for cooperation with the States; provides for technical advice and training to other countries; and repeals effective parts of the Acts of 1966 and 1969.
3. Summary of environmental impact and adverse environmental effects:
Impact on endangered species as to actual changes in numbers will vary from
little with species which are only threatened and not depleted when the
program has its effect to many-fold increase with species that are returned
from the brink of extinction back to a viable role in the ecosystem. There
will be some significant impact on the environment of the species when forage
or prey populations adjust to accommodate increased populations of the\nendangered species. Economic impacts will occur-negative where use of a
species is lost and positive where it is regained. Impacts will occur in the
cost of resources lost or altered to make room for endangered species restoration. Social impacts will appear when endangered animals become vectors of
human disease; when people receive satisfaction in the protection and restoration of endangered species and in the preservation of the strength and meaning
of symbols depicted by endangered animals saved from extinction.
Adverse effects will be sustained by people subject to punishment for violation of the law; by land developers who must forego development of lands needed for endangered species; by States which lose authority to regulate taking of endangered species; by people who must forego economic gain when products from endangered species are no longer legally marketable; by farmers and ranchers who suffer crop or livestock depredations by endangered animals; and by Federal agencies which sustain added costs of decisions favorable to endangered species.
